briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax Relief in Sight, Psychedelics Breakthroughs Mount: Industry Keeps Moving
briefs.top: Michigan operators are getting real signals of relief as the governor's race turns into a referendum on the 24% wholesale tax, even as regulators keep cleaning house on bad actors. Nationally, Compass Pathways is sprinting toward a historic FDA psychedelic approval and M&A is heating up from Curaleaf to Spherex, while federal rescheduling hits a procedural — not fatal — pause.

local.text: Bay City turns weed tax dollars into shelter beds — City commissioners are set to approve $150,000 in local marijuana tax revenue to keep an overnight homeless drop-in center open for another year.

Industry rallies behind a tax-repeal candidate for governor — The Michigan Cannabis Industry Association has officially endorsed GOP nominee John James after he pledged to repeal or sharply cut the 24% wholesale tax crushing operators.
Next wholesale tax payment due in two weeks — Michigan cannabis businesses owe their next quarterly 24% wholesale tax installment to Treasury by Oct. 20, part of the 2026 good-faith payment schedule.

Regulators clear the air for compliant operators — State regulators revoked 20 cultivation licenses and fined one company $2 million for shipping product labeled as marijuana that actually contained dirt and mulch, while also pulling Muha Meds' Ypsilanti dispensary license and fining it $250,000 for running a fake customer profile.

Judge rules against grower over wetlands destruction — A judge found Bliss Cannabis illegally destroyed 16 acres of protected wetlands in Iosco County to build a cultivation site, with penalties to be decided next month.

national.text: Compass Pathways opens new HQ, nears historic FDA milestone — The psilocybin developer opened a new U.S. headquarters in Jersey City as it moves closer to launching COMP360 for treatment-resistant depression, with a U.S. debut anticipated in the first half of 2027 that would mark the first FDA-approved psychedelic drug.

DEA opens new registration path for medical cannabis firms — The agency's Diversion Control Division launched a fresh Form 225 application process so state-licensed medical cannabis manufacturers, distributors and labs can register for Schedule III protections.

Curaleaf raises the stakes in its Aurora takeover bid — The multistate operator sweetened its offer to roughly $5 per share, representing an 86% premium, as it pushes to combine with Canada's Aurora Cannabis.

Spherex goes vertical with first-ever acquisition — Colorado's top cannabis brand agreed to buy two cultivation facilities from The Cannabist Company, a deal set to more than double Spherex's workforce.

Rescheduling hits a procedural pause, not a dead end — A DEA judge stayed the Schedule III hearing to weigh a new GAO report, with the government's response due Oct. 13 and the stay explicitly not affecting the April order already covering state-licensed medical marijuana.
